Subject: Request: Helios Labs — 3yr rate anchor, uplift fence & renewal parity

Team,

Quick background: Helios Labs (prospect -> high-probability close) is asking for a three‑year commitment with a 40% first‑year effective discount (applied via a blended usage tier), a contractual price anchor for years 1–3 (no increases to baseline unit pricing), and an "uplift fence" that caps annual list increases on renewals to a fixed percent (they proposed 8%/yr). They also want a renewal parity clause: if their usage grows by >30% at renewal, they ask for protection so they can't be repriced materially above the anchor for the first renewal.

Why this matters: This buyer is strategic for our life sciences vertical and will be a reference for multi‑model inference throughput (expected initial committed spend $1.2M ARR). If we approve the anchor + uplift fence, we reduce churn risk and make the economics predictable for Helios. If we deny, risk of losing the deal to a competitor who will offer more aggressive term stability is high.

Ask: I need a deal desk / exec exception for the following non‑standard terms:
- 36‑month term with 40% blended first‑year discount (linked to usage tiers)
- Price anchor for base token/unit rates for years 1–3 (no increases to baseline rates)
- Uplift cap of 8%/year on list price for renewal adjustments (cap negotiable)
- Renewal parity protection for first renewal (usage growth carveout, limits on material repricing)

Attachments: Helios_MA‑v3‑redlines.pdf (their redlines), Helios_Q3_usage_snapshot.csv (pilot usage).

Please reply with: approve / conditional approve (and what condition) / deny. If approved, I will route to legal for redline reconciliation and get signatures.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Request: Helios Labs — 3yr rate anchor, uplift fence & renewal parity

Thanks Vanessa — reviewed the ask and poked through the numbers. Short assessment:

- Upside: $1.2M ARR committed initially, strong logo, expected expansion runway after year 1.
- Downside: 3yr anchor + 40% blended discount materially reduces realized ASP vs list in years 1–2; uplift cap at 8% slows our ability to recover list if macro pricing rises.
- Risk control levers we can offer: step‑up floors, usage banding for uplift applicability (only above baseline growth), and a 1yr performance SLAs tied to partial clawback on deep discounts.

My suggested conditional approval for deal desk:
1) Approve 36mo term with 40% blended first‑year discount if Helios agrees to a 12% minimum uplift band on any renewal pricing that applies only if they exceed a defined growth threshold (we'd propose 'growth above 30%').
2) If they insist on an 8% hard cap, require a revenue share overage clause for any usage >x% and a pilot window (90 days) with minimum throughput commitments.
3) Legal to add a sunset that allows repricing after year 3 if macro cost index (to be defined) increases >15%.

I attached a one‑page Deal_Summary_HL‑2027‑09.xlsx with modeled impacts at different uplift caps.

If leadership buys the 12% floor instead of the 8% cap, the margin delta is reasonable and we can accept the anchor. Otherwise we should push for the pilot + overage.

—Marissa

Team — I read the summary and the attached modeling. I will approve an exception here with the following conditions:

1) Uplift cap: approve a flexible cap at 10%/yr. No lower hard cap (i.e., not 8%).
2) Performance pilot: 90‑day pilot required, with measurable throughput milestones. If milestones are missed, we reserve the right to reduce the effective discount.
3) Renewal parity: limited to first renewal only; exclude any clause that prohibits reasonable market repricing beyond year 3.
4) Legal to finalize a revenue share for overages beyond the committed band (suggest 65/35).

This balances the customer ask with protecting our long‑term ASP. Marcus/Ben — move forward with Vanessa to confirm Helios accepts these conditions; legal will be on standby to incorporate into the MSA. Aditya — please run final P&L / NPV so we have a finance signoff before DocuSign.
